source: Current local Windows TCP and UDP endpoint tables

provider_reconciliation.endpoint_identity: Address family, transport, local address/port/scope, and for TCP the remote address/port/scope. PID is not used alone as identity.
provider_reconciliation.tcp: Provider rows with the same TCP 4-tuple are merged; owner/state conflicts are retained.
provider_reconciliation.udp: Matching local endpoint rows are merged when ownership agrees or one provider has no PID; distinct known owners are retained.
provider_reconciliation.provider_disagreements: All conflicting provider field values are retained separately in the top-level provider_disagreements section; these are observations, not collection errors.

address_family_protocol_local_remote.supported_conditions: IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP rows returned during each provider query.
address_family_protocol_local_remote.unavailability: Provider failure, malformed records, or live endpoint changes; UDP remote peer is not applicable.

ipv6_scope_ids.provider: psutil IPv6 address tuple and IP Helper IPv6 owner-module rows
ipv6_scope_ids.supported_conditions: IPv6 endpoints; IP Helper scope IDs and network byte order are converted to host-order integers.
ipv6_scope_ids.unavailability: Not applicable to IPv4; null only when a source does not expose the scope value.

tcp_state.supported_conditions: TCP endpoints; API state numbers are mapped to documented Windows state names.
tcp_state.unavailability: Not applicable to UDP; unknown numeric Windows state is retained as UNKNOWN_<number>.

owning_pid.provider: Windows IP Helper owner-module tables and psutil endpoint pid
owning_pid.supported_conditions: PID is available; PID 0 is retained for TCP, while Microsoft defines UDP PID 0 as unavailable.
owning_pid.unavailability: Provider access/visibility limits; null with a field_unavailability explanation or field error where available.

process_metadata.supported_conditions: Owner PID is available and field access succeeds; PID creation time is checked before/after lookup.
process_metadata.unavailability: Access denied, process exit, PID reuse, or provider error; null with field-level status/error. System Idle Process executable path is marked not applicable.

field_unavailability.provider: Windows APIs and psutil field lookups
field_unavailability.supported_conditions: Unavailable optional fields retain a field_unavailability explanation without being reported as collector failures.
field_unavailability.unavailability: Access denied, process exit, endpoint disappearance during module lookup, and not-applicable fields are limitations; unexpected provider failures remain in errors.

process_creation_time.supported_conditions: Returned value is recorded both as Unix epoch seconds and UTC ISO 8601.
process_creation_time.unavailability: Owner process exited, access was denied, or PID identity changed during lookup.

endpoint_creation_time_utc.supported_conditions: The Windows row supplies the context-bind creation timestamp; the original 100-nanosecond FILETIME integer and converted UTC timestamp are both retained.
endpoint_creation_time_utc.unavailability: Null for psutil-only records or when the provider row/timestamp is unavailable or invalid. This is a context-bind timestamp, not necessarily the moment application data began.

endpoint_creation_time_filetime_100ns.supported_conditions: The original unsigned FILETIME tick value is retained alongside its UTC conversion.
endpoint_creation_time_filetime_100ns.unavailability: Null when the owner-module timestamp is unavailable or invalid.

owning_module_info.supported_conditions: When the owner-module endpoint row is returned and Windows resolves module name and/or full path.
owning_module_info.unavailability: Null with a field_unavailability reason when the endpoint changes before resolution or Windows supplies no module strings; API failures are retained as field errors.

first_observed_at_utc_last_observed_at_u.provider: Collector observation time while each provider row is enumerated
first_observed_at_utc_last_observed_at_u.supported_conditions: Records when this endpoint tuple was observed during this single acquisition; duplicate provider observations are combined using earliest/latest observation times.
first_observed_at_utc_last_observed_at_u.unavailability: These fields do not imply historical monitoring, and do not establish actual endpoint creation or lifetime.

application_protocol_hint.supported_conditions: A recognized transport/port tuple yields one or more candidates marked unconfirmed.
application_protocol_hint.unavailability: No hint when the port is unmapped. No packets, payloads, TLS metadata, or application protocol negotiation are inspected.

socket_descriptor.supported_conditions: Only when psutil returns a non-negative descriptor.
socket_descriptor.unavailability: Windows commonly supplies -1; then value is null and status is unsupported.

limitations: This is a live snapshot. Connections and owners can change while providers are queried.
The IP Helper tables are queried separately and are not an atomic snapshot with psutil.
Process metadata is a later best-effort lookup; PID reuse is checked using process creation time but cannot be made race-free.
Administrator privileges can improve visibility but do not guarantee access to every owner field.
Owner-module APIs provide context-bind FILETIME and best-effort module name/path, not a guarantee of the application component responsible for all traffic.
First/last observed timestamps cover only the observations made within this one acquisition; no monitoring or historical closed-connection collection is performed.
Application-protocol hints are unconfirmed port-based candidates, not protocol identification; no packet contents or traffic indicators are collected.
Windows endpoint tables do not provide packet contents, byte counts, or historical connections.
UDP records do not identify a remote peer; UDP state is not applicable.
An endpoint port number does not prove an application-layer protocol.
